question_text: Evaluate lim(x → a) (sin(x − a) · tan²(x − a))/((x² − a²)²).

mark_split.label: Apply the standard limits and substitute

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how many powers of (x − a) sit above and below, and what is left over.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Count the powers of (x − a)
steps.margin_note: First mark. Above: sin gives one power and tan² gives two, so three in all. Below: (x² − a²)² = (x − a)²(x + a)² gives only two. One power of (x − a) is therefore left in the numerator.
lines: At x = a both the numerator and the denominator are 0, so the form is 0/0. Take a ≠ 0.
The numerator sin(x − a) · tan²(x − a) behaves like (x − a)³ near x = a: three powers.
The denominator is  (x² − a²)² = (x − a)²(x + a)²:  two powers of (x − a).
[sin(x − a)/(x − a)] · [tan(x − a)/(x − a)]² · (x − a)/(x + a)²

recall.must_convey: That the numerator carries three powers of (x − a) and the denominator two, leaving one power of (x − a) over.
accept: three powers on top and two below so one x minus a is left over
sin gives one power and tan squared gives two
x squared minus a squared all squared has only two factors of x minus a
paiki moodu powers, kinda rendu powers, oka x minus a migulutundi

steps.why: Whether such a limit is a number or 0 is settled entirely by the count of factors, so counting before cancelling is what decides the whole answer. Here the count is 3 above against 2 below.
common_mistakes: Reading (x² − a²)² as carrying four powers of (x − a).
Cancelling all three powers above against the two below and answering 1/(2a)².
steps.memory_tip: Square the factorisation first: (x² − a²)² = (x − a)²(x + a)². Only then are the two powers of (x − a) visible.

steps.label: Apply the standard limits and substitute
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The two bracketed quotients tend to 1, and the leftover factor (x − a)/(x + a)² tends to 0/(2a)². The answer is 0.
lines: As x → a, the angle (x − a) → 0, so
lim sin(x − a)/(x − a) = 1   and   lim [tan(x − a)/(x − a)]² = 1² = 1
The remaining factor is continuous at x = a, so substitute x = a:

lines.text: ∴ lim(x → a) (sin(x − a) · tan²(x − a))/((x² − a²)²) = 0,  a ≠ 0

recall.must_convey: That both standard limits give 1 and the leftover factor (x − a)/(x + a)² tends to 0, so the limit is 0.
accept: the two brackets are one and the leftover x minus a goes to zero
the extra power of x minus a makes the whole thing vanish
migilina x minus a zero avuthundi kabatti answer zero
the limit is zero because the top has a higher order

steps.why: The numerator is of higher order than the denominator, so the quotient is driven to 0 rather than to a finite non-zero value. The value checks numerically: with a = 2 the expression is 0.000622 at x = 2.01 and 0.0000625 at x = 2.001, falling by a factor of ten each time, exactly as (x − a)/(2a)² = (x − a)/16 does.
common_mistakes: Answering 1/(4a²) by cancelling one power of (x − a) too many.
Writing the answer as 1/(2a)³ by copying the pattern of the simpler tangent question.
steps.memory_tip: When the numerator carries more powers of (x − a) than the denominator, the limit is 0. Only equal counts give a non-zero number.

insider_note: Count powers of (x − a): three on top, two below, so one survives and drives the answer to 0. A limit of 0 is the correct answer here, not a sign of a mistake.
